explanation: A people group who lived in Canaan and were enemies of Israel during several periods of history.
Also called the "Ark of the Covenant," a holy chest that contained the stone tablets with the Ten Commandments, and represented God's presence among the Israelites.
The chief god of the Philistines, often associated with fertility and grain.
One of the most important cities of the Philistines, mentioned several times in 1 Samuel 6.
Another major Philistine city, where the Ark was first brought after the Philistines captured it from the Israelites.
Plagues that struck the Philistines as a result of taking the Ark. May refer to a form of boils or swellings.
Offerings made by the Philistines in gold to make peace with God after taking the Ark and suffering under plagues.
A city in Judah where the Ark was returned to the Israelites after the Philistines sent it back on a cart pulled by cows.
